x: It was good to see Derek Crookes fully recovered from his serious illness and to witness John Hilton's pleasure in clocking his best time to date.

John Hilton finished in his best time to date in front of Charlie Walker and Pete Sadler who were well up at one point but fell away towards the end Reg Hopkins and Wally Wortley completed our ten finishers.
Pete Sadler,Norman Stairs and John Hilton finished 16th,18th and 37th with times of 56:24,56:42 and 61:39 respectively,all of which qualify towards 2nd class standards.
By his runs in the Mitcham '15',Epsom '10' and Finchley '20' John Hilton became the first member to obtain the newly instituted 2nd class Road Running Standard.

The Belgrave Team,running as Cadogan AC,finished 3rd in the Middlesex '20',held in conjunction with the Finchley Open '20'. John Hilton, Geoff Pearson and Ken Stimpson comprised the team . John's time completed his qualification for our 2nd class standard.

After going through 15miles in just over 84mins. he began to slow down quite a bit and John Moore, now beginning to get a little fitter, passed Charlie at about 21 miles and went on to take the Belgrave Championship Geoff Pearson and John Hilton ran well throughout John finishing in a personal best time.
Unfortunately Charlie was forced to retire at 20 miles and join the other victims, Norman Stairs and John Hilton thus leaving Geoff Pearson and Ken Stimpson to close in the team.
BOTTOM CENTRE: Lionel Mann and Chris Steer having their usual private duel. BOTTOM RIGHT: John Hilton.
The Bels "A" squad of Charlie Dabbs - another to move through strongly as the race went on, finishing up in 7th place - Lionel Mann, 15th, and John Hilton, 44th, was fourth.

Surprises in the middle of the field were Chris Fairfield, John Hilton and our veteran ex marathon champion Colin Collis. Battling together for much of the race these three didn't realise they were fighting for two of the handicap prizes!
